data.name: Hera
data.gender_notes: Hera is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Goddess of marriage, childbirth, and women
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Hera is the queen of the gods and goddess of marriage, childbirth, women, child rearing, and family. She is the protector of homes and the goddess of hearth, the wife and partner of Zeus. The name Hera carries the meaning “Goddess of marriage, childbirth, and women” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hera usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of marriage, childbirth, and women and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of maternal love, protection, and divine grace.
data.etymology: Hera belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of marriage, childbirth, and women.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hera total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Hera, named after the Greek goddess, has been used as a given name for centuries. Nowadays, it's more commonly found among Christians in Greece and countries with a significant Greek cultural influence. Her name symbolizes a connection to ancient Greek culture, and for many, it's a tribute to the strength, power, and nurturing qualities associated with the goddess.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Hera can be seen as a reminder of the divine protection and support offered by the holy family in raising children and strengthening marriages and families. Her name counters societal pressures and maintains an appreciation for the sanctity of traditional roles, values, and relationships. Through this name, Christians can seek guidance from the spiritual and symbolic meanings of the Greek goddess Hera.
